newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SPAIN BEAT AUSTRALIA TO STAY IN FED CUP WORLD GROUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN BEAT AUSTRALIA TO STAY IN FED CUP WORLD GROUP.

text.p: Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Maria Luisa Serna won their reverse singles matches on Sunday to lift Spain to a 3-2 victory over Australia in their Fed Cup world group play-off.
The win means Spain stay in the elite eight-nation world group next season while Australia must remain in group two.

Former world number one Sanchez Vicario outclassed Australia's top player Annabel Ellwood to win 6-2 6-0 before Serna gave the visitors an unassailable 3-1 lead when she beat Rachel McQuillan 6-1 6-3.
Australian pair Kerry-Anne Guse and Kristine Kunce then teamed up to win the doubles match 6-2 6-4 over the Spanish combination of Cristina Torrens-Valero and Maria Antonia Sanchez Lorenzo.
Sanchez Vicario disposed of her two singles opponents during the two-day tie for the loss of just five games but Serna admitted to suffering from a severe attack of nerves.
The 18-year-old Serna was called into the Spanish line-up only after former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez opted not to compete on the hardcourts at the Hope Island resort in Queensland state.
Serna broke down in tears after losing her opening singles match on Saturday to leave the teams locked at 1-1 overnight but she was a different player when the tie resumed on Sunday.
"I'm supposed to be playing for Conchita Martinez and it was very hard for me," Serna said.
"But I think that I played very well and showed that Spain also has more players than just Arantxa and Conchita."
